subject.title: [Security] Missing CSRF protection on local control plane HTTP routes

question: Should every browser-origin state-changing Gateway HTTP route enforce a centralized Origin/Fetch-Metadata policy beyond existing route authentication, and which native or proxy callers must remain exempt?
rationale: Source inspection establishes related defenses and authenticated HTTP surfaces, but choosing a universal browser-origin boundary requires maintainer intent about no-auth loopback use, trusted proxies, plugins, and non-browser compatibility.

options.title: Audit and centralize origin policy
options.body: Inventory the active routes and apply one shared browser-origin gate only where the authentication and client contracts require it.

options.title: Keep authentication as the boundary
options.body: Confirm that all state-changing HTTP routes require non-ambient operator credentials and document why classic CSRF is not applicable.

options.title: Require per-route CSRF tokens
options.body: Add explicit anti-CSRF tokens to browser-facing mutation routes, accepting the additional client and upgrade complexity.

recommendation.title: Audit and centralize origin policy
recommendation.body: Inventory the active routes and apply one shared browser-origin gate only where the authentication and client contracts require it.

likelyOwner.reason: The closest merged browser-origin hardening was co-authored and merged by this contributor, including compatibility handling for legitimate loopback clients.
